label: Bible Study
prompt: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above _____.
verse: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
note: The opening line of the virtuous woman poem — an acrostic running through the Hebrew alphabet.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my _____, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
verse: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
note: Quoting Psalm 118, the writer turns 'I will not fear' into something we can boldly say out loud.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven _____, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
verse: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
note: Pharaoh retells his dream to Joseph: seven fat 'kine' — old English for cows — soon to be eaten by seven lean ones.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye _____ thee.
verse: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
note: Job's final confession: after all the debate, secondhand theology gave way to sight.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Because _____ is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
verse: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
note: 'Strait' means tight and narrow, as in straitjacket — not 'straight.' The KJV gate is cramped, not level.
